title: CogmemAi Scores 91% on LoCoMo — Above Human Performance
content:
The Benchmark That Matters

The LoCoMo benchmark is the industry standard for testing how well Ai memory systems recall information from long conversations. Created by Snap Research and published at ACL 2024, it tests five critical capabilities: single-hop fact recall, temporal reasoning, multi-hop inference, world knowledge, and adversarial question handling.

Human performance on LoCoMo is 87.9%.

CogmemAi scores 91%.

CogmemAi's recall engine now outperforms human memory on this benchmark, with 100% retrieval hit rate and particularly strong performance in world knowledge (100%) and temporal reasoning (97.3%).

What This Means For You

When your Ai coding assistant uses CogmemAi, it remembers your conversations better than you do. Architecture decisions from three months ago, that bug fix from last Tuesday, the deployment process your teammate explained last week — CogmemAi finds it when you need it.

This isn't theoretical. The LoCoMo benchmark tests real conversational recall across dozens of sessions spanning months of conversation history. The questions range from simple fact lookups to complex temporal calculations to multi-step reasoning chains. CogmemAi handles them all.

The Dirty Secret of Ai Memory Benchmarks

Here's something the industry doesn't want you to know: benchmark scores across different Ai memory systems are not comparable.

Every vendor runs their own evaluation using different configurations:

  • Different answering models (some use the latest, most expensive models to inflate scores)
  • Different judge models (the model that decides if an answer is "correct")
  • Different evaluation prompts (some are generous, some are strict)
  • Different question subsets (some skip the hardest categories entirely)

One vendor jumped 7 percentage points overnight — not by improving their memory system, but by upgrading the model that generates answers. The memory system was the same. The brain doing the answering was smarter. They claimed the improvement as a memory breakthrough.

Another vendor's widely-cited score turns out to be from a completely different benchmark, not LoCoMo at all.

None of the top scores in this space come from peer-reviewed research. Every vendor evaluates themselves using their own tools.

How CogmemAi's Score Was Achieved

We believe in transparency. Here's exactly how we got 91%:

  • 100 questions from the LoCoMo dataset
  • Claude Opus 4.6 for both answering and judging (same model, consistent methodology)
  • Full conversation storage — we store the complete, unmodified conversation text. No preprocessing, no paraphrasing, no lossy compression
  • Semantic search + keyword search fused together for retrieval
  • Precision reranking to surface the most relevant memories first
  • Think Before You Speak — our system checks what it already knows before suggesting anything

We don't game the test. We store the data verbatim and let our recall engine do the work.

The Philosophy Behind 91%

Our approach is simple: store everything, search well, use the best brain.

We tried the complicated approaches — extracting facts, generating question-answer pairs, chunking conversations into tiny pieces, having models rewrite and summarize. Every layer of processing corrupted the original data. Details got lost, words got changed, context got broken.

The breakthrough came when we stopped trying to be clever about storage and focused on being excellent at retrieval. Store the conversation as it happened. Build a retrieval engine that finds the right memory when asked. Let the most capable Ai model reason over the results.

Simple beats clever. Every time.

What's Next

91% is not the finish line. Our single-hop fact recall still has room to improve, and we're continuing to refine our retrieval engine and answer quality. But we're not chasing inflated benchmark numbers. We're building the memory system that works best in real-world Ai workflows.

Store everything. Search well. Use the best brain. Remember everything.
